title: serving-runtime-daily-scratchpad-2026-03-27
content:
Morning triage notes (quick)
- Spike yesterday: latency regression noticed in canary after kernel change (PR #1428). P50 ~+12ms, P95 ~+80ms on long-context traces.
- INF-4123: memory leak in kv-cache path when sequence_length > 4096 (repro on rtx-a100-80gb). Reproduced locally with batch=8 + long warmups.
- Priority: stabilize canary -> rollback or soft-fix? we need to decide before EOD.

What I ran this morning
- repro script: ./tools/repro/kv-leak.sh --model redwood-mix-13b --seq 8192 --batch 8
- perf snapshot: ./scripts/collect-nsys.sh canary-node-7 -> saved to /tmp/nsys-canary-2026-03-27.qdrep
- pprof on runtime: go tool pprof -http=:8081 svc:9090/profile?seconds=30 -> saw growing heap alloc in cache/kv_store.go

Quick findings
- Leak seems tied to LRU eviction path hitting when prefix cache populated + continuous streaming. Suspect reference counting bug around pinned entries (cache.pin()).
- Kernel change in PR #1428 adds an extra memcpy in attention kernel for long kv sequences; might be increasing CPU contention and causing slower GC cycles (observed in flame graph).
- Repro with quantized model (q4f) reduces memory pressure and leak not immediately visible -> temporary mitigation: route long-context requests to quantized variant behind fallback policy.

Actionable TODOs
- [high] Revert PR #1428 on canary and run 6-hour soak. Owner: Priya. Target: 2026-03-27 15:30 PT.
- [high] Add defensive nil-check + decrement logic in cache.pin() (small patch) to prevent double-claim. Owner: me (Jordan). Patch + unit test by EOD.
- [medium] Add metric (cache.pinned_count) + alert if > threshold for >5m. Owner: SRE (Liam) -> create INF follow-up.
- [medium] Update routing: enable fallback to q4f variant for seq>4096. Work with product to approve.
- [low] Add e2e test for long-context streaming (batch 8, seq 8192) to catch memory growth in CI (nightly).

Kernel/perf notes (reminder)
- Revisit kernel memcpy in attn_long_seq_kern.c: attempt to replace with in-place pointer shuffle to avoid extra allocs. Benchmark: 1) current, 2) memcpy removed, 3) hw-accelerated copy (cudaMemcpyAsync).
- Check nvprof/nsys for GPU memcpy stalls and CPU->GPU sync points. Observed spikes at token boundary where cached KV is merged.
- Run micro-bench: scripts/bench/attention_longseq.py --repeats 100 --seq 8192 --kcache true --use-memcpy true/false

Notes to self / meeting prep
- 11:00 sync w/ Priya & Liam: present repro, show flamegraph, propose revert + patch plan.
- 14:00 standup: ask product about acceptable fallback to q4f for enterprise customers (impacts SLOs?).
- Draft for ops runbook: "if canary latency reg > baseline +20% -> auto rollback + open INF ticket". Need SRE buy-in.

Investigation logs / useful commands
- tail -f /var/log/serving/runtime.log | grep "kv-cache"
- go test ./cache -run TestPinUnpin -v -race
- sudo nsys profile --output /tmp/nsys-canary -t cuda,osrt --sample 100 --duration 60 --processes 12345
- pprof heap: curl "http://127.0.0.1:9090/debug/pprof/heap" > /tmp/heap.pb && go tool pprof -alloc_space /usr/bin/serving /tmp/heap.pb

Open questions
- Is the memcpy necessary for correctness on some topologies (e.g., bert-like layouts)? Need to check with kernel author (Alex).
- Can we express a routing policy that targets quantized fallback only for long-context and non-SLA-critical customers? (product + sales input).

Small wins to ship quickly
- Add unit test for double-unpin in cache (15-30m).
- Add canary alert threshold for locked memory > 2GB above baseline (SRE).

Random notes / brain dump
- If we gate revert on additional tests, add smoke that streams for 10s with seq=8192 after deploy.
- Keep an eye on customer 47 (enterprise) who rolled out yesterday; might be affected. Slack DM them proactively if rollback happens.

End of scratchpad - will update after 11:00 sync.
